local_review.finding_body: The new-library contribution reports 0/2 dynamic-access coverage, violating §FS-contribution-contract.3. The coverage report identifies both calls as Class.getDeclaredField and Field.get in SystemLambda$WithEnvironmentVariables.getFieldValue (SystemLambda.java:1379-1381). That public path reflectively mutates System.getenv() internals. Native execution evidence shows NoSuchFieldException for field m on the substituted environment map and, with the field registered, InaccessibleObjectException for java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableMap.m because java.base does not open java.util. Thus all library dynamic access is behind JDK-internal behavior Native Image substitutes or withholds, and no metadata entry can satisfy the coverage gate. Under §FS-contribution-contract.5.4, this previously unindexed new library leaves nothing to record and must be closed.
local_review.finding_title: System Lambda 1.2.1 dynamic access is unsupported by Native Image
local_review.review_comment: Reviewed the single-coordinate diff, test contract, local gate evidence, resolved statistics, and all three finalization lanes. The test is meaningful, version-agnostic, separately packaged, and passes JVM and Native Image execution, but the reported dynamic-access coverage is 0/2. Both tracked calls are in WithEnvironmentVariables.getFieldValue and exist solely to reflect into System.getenv() JDK internals. Native Image substitutes/withholds that state: runs first failed because the substituted environment map had no field m, and after registration failed with InaccessibleObjectException for java.util.Collections$UnmodifiableMap.m. Metadata cannot make this environment-mutation path supported, so the >20% new-library gate is unreachable. The artifact has no index entry in the base tree, leaving no skip record to merge; §FS-contribution-contract.5.4 therefore requires closure.
